evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 形義通解; graphic analysis and historical usage
evidence.text: CUHK says 再’s oracle and bronze construction and original meaning are unsettled. It reports competing proposals: Xu Zhongshu’s fish interpretation, with 冓 as two fish meeting (but the graph differs from 魚 and the proposal remains unverified); Shirakawa Shizuka’s cord-making tool interpretation; and Xu Shen’s account of one act yielding two, hence two/repetition. Warring States forms may add 二 or 口 decoratively, with 二 possibly also contributing the meaning ‘two’. The oracle-bone context is fragmentary and unclear. CUHK reports bronze uses for ‘second time/again’ (陳璋方壺; 叔尸鐘) and ‘two’ (𠫑羌鐘, twenty-two), Warring States bamboo use 再三, and a possible whole-graph loan for 在 in a Guodian slip, marked as uncertain.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「再」

evidence.field: File description; Summary, Source, Licensing, file link
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 再-seal.svg as a digitally created vector depicting 再 in Shuowen seal-script style. It identifies S02855 on hanziyuan.net as the source for the drawing and releases the SVG representation under a public-domain dedication. This is a modern redraw of a script form, not a photograph or facsimile of an ancient artifact. The page links the original image file directly.

evidence.field: entry metadata; script examples and historical phonology
evidence.text: The character entry identifies 再 as U+518D, gives modern Mandarin zài and Guangyun fanqie 作代, and displays small-seal, bronze, oracle-bone, and manuscript examples. Its explanatory text says the graph’s original construction is unsettled; therefore these forms and readings do not establish a component as phonetic.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「再」

evidence.text: The secondary table gives 再 Mandarin zài, Middle Chinese ‹tsojH›, and Old Chinese /*[ts]ˤə(ʔ)-s/ in the Baxter–Sagart system; it separately gives Zhengzhang /*ʔsɯːs/. These are different reconstruction systems, not interchangeable transcriptions. The local exact Baxter–Sagart row supplied in the packet agrees for 再; local 冓 has Mandarin gòu, MC kuwH, OC *kˤ(r)o-s, gloss 中冓 ‘inner chamber’. This does not support a phonetic role for 冓 in 再. The local values are repository rows, not claims read from an upstream table.

search_audit.outcome: Search performed. Opened the exact Commons file page and CUHK graph-analysis page. CUHK supports competing analyses and early uses, while explicitly leaving construction uncertain. Commons page establishes a modern seal-style drawing and public-domain rights.

search_audit.query: Unicode Unihan 再 U+518D Unihan; Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang 再 字形 演變 record; 再 冓 pronunciation Baxter Sagart 2014 *[ts]ˤə(ʔ)-s *kˤ(r)o-s
search_audit.outcome: Both exact Unicode Unihan record URLs were attempted and returned internal errors. Xiaoxuetang query opened but no individual glyph records were visible. Wiktionary’s pronunciation table was inspected for a secondary transcription cross-check.

search_audit.query: No separate search; followed links from the inspected Commons description to Sinica, Chinese Etymology, and CUHK pages
search_audit.outcome: Opened the cited database pages. CUHK’s entry was inspected directly. Xiaoxuetang did not expose result glyphs in rendered page content; Hanziyuan landing page displayed examples for another character rather than a character-specific result, so it was not used as evidence about 再.

gaps: The original referent and the graphic relation of 再’s parts to 魚, 冓, 一, and 二 remain disputed. No sound-component analysis is supported; 冓’s checked readings are recorded separately and do not make it phonetic in this graph.

The relationship between the fragmentary oracle-bone contexts and the later bronze meanings is not established by the inspected pages. CUHK reports early bronze uses for ‘again/second time’ and ‘two’, plus a possible whole-graph loan for 在; the loan reading is explicitly uncertain. The spoken word’s earliest attestation and a complete chronology of sense extensions remain unknown.

The CUHK page names inscription and manuscript examples but does not provide absolute dates for each object or text. A full form-by-form transition sequence and any proposed corruption are not established; no corruption claim is made.
The character-specific page for 冓 was not independently opened in this pass; the supplied local rows were checked, and the Unicode record attempt failed. No external reading claim for 冓 is made.

Xiaoxuetang’s page rendered without its character-specific result list in the accessible web tool. The Commons description’s cited Sears character image does not establish artifact provenance for the seal-style redraw. The selected glyph is explanatory evidence for a later script style only, not for ancient graphic evolution.

No external license terms for bulk text reuse were investigated or proposed; the evidence is limited to concise character-specific paraphrase and the selected Commons image’s stated public-domain release.
